title: The Glory of the LORD Filled the Tabernacle
theme: On the first day of the new year, Moses sets up the tabernacle and places everything in it as God commanded, anoints it and prepares the priests. When the work is finished, the cloud covers the tent and the glory of the LORD fills it, so that even Moses cannot enter. From then on the cloud leads Israel in all their journeys.

language.note: Moses 'raised up' the tabernacle. The verb is used of setting up a monument or establishing a covenant. God's dwelling now stands among his people.
'So Moses finished the work.' Like Genesis 2:2, 'God finished his work.' Completion is followed immediately by God's presence, as creation was followed by God's rest.
'The cloud settled on it.' The verb behind mishkan (tabernacle) and the later Jewish term Shekinah, God's dwelling presence. The promise of 25:8 and 29:45 is fulfilled: God dwells among them.

'The glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.' Fullness of glory is the goal of the whole book. The same happens at the dedication of Solomon's temple (1 Kings 8:10-11), and Isaiah sees the whole earth full of his glory (Isaiah 6:3).
'Throughout all their journeys.' When the cloud lifted, Israel set out; when it stayed, they stayed. God's presence now travels with his people toward the promised land.

usage.note: The glory fills Solomon's temple, departs before the exile (Ezekiel 10), and is promised to return. Haggai says the latter glory of God's house will be greater than the former.
'The Word became flesh and dwelt (tabernacled) among us, and we have seen his glory.' Jesus calls his body the temple. In him the whole fullness of deity dwells bodily.
Believers are God's temple, in whom his Spirit dwells, being built together into a dwelling place for God.
'Behold, the dwelling place (tabernacle) of God is with man.' In the new Jerusalem there is no temple, for God and the Lamb are its temple, and his glory is its light.

context.setting: Almost a year after the exodus (v17; compare 12:2 and 19:1), on the first day of the first month of the second year, the tabernacle is erected. Exodus ends where it has been heading: God dwelling among his redeemed people. Leviticus begins with God calling to Moses from this tent, and Numbers picks up the cloud's guidance.

flow.label: God's instructions
flow.note: God commands Moses to erect the tabernacle on New Year's Day, set the furniture in place, anoint everything, and wash, clothe and anoint Aaron and his sons for a lasting priesthood.

flow.label: Moses sets it up
flow.note: Moses does everything as the LORD commanded: frames and coverings, the ark with the testimony behind the veil, the table, lampstand, golden altar, screen, bronze altar, basin and court. So Moses finished the work.

flow.label: The glory fills the tabernacle
flow.note: The cloud covers the tent of meeting and the glory of the LORD fills the tabernacle. Moses cannot enter because the cloud has settled on it.

flow.label: The cloud leads
flow.note: Whenever the cloud lifts, Israel sets out; when it does not, they stay. Cloud by day and fire by night are over the tabernacle in the sight of all Israel throughout their journeys.

tier1.note: When Solomon dedicates the temple, the cloud fills it and the priests cannot stand to minister because of the glory.
The cloud's guidance is described in detail: at the LORD's command they camped, at his command they set out.
The next book opens with God calling to Moses from the tent he could not enter.

tier2.note: John uses the verb for pitching a tent: the Word tabernacled among us, and we saw his glory.
Ezekiel sees the glory leave the temple and later return to fill it.
The story ends with God's tabernacle with humanity, a dwelling that never departs.

tier3.note: At Pentecost the Spirit fills the house where the disciples are gathered and rests on each, making them God's dwelling.
Believers behold the glory of the Lord and are transformed from one degree of glory to another.
All who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God, guided as Israel was by the cloud.

voices.name: T. Desmond Alexander
voices.work: From Paradise to the Promised Land
voices.view: Alexander sees the glory filling the tabernacle as the climax of Exodus. The book moves from Israel serving Pharaoh to God dwelling among his people, and this restoration of God's presence is a major step in the Bible's story from Eden to the new Jerusalem.

voices.name: G. K. Beale
voices.work: The Temple and the Church's Mission
voices.view: Beale argues that the glory filling the tabernacle anticipates God's purpose to fill the whole earth with his presence. The tabernacle is a beachhead of new creation, extended through Christ and the church until the whole creation becomes God's temple.

voices.name: BibleProject (Tim Mackie)
voices.view: BibleProject ends its Exodus overview by noting that God's glory now dwells in the tent at the center of Israel's camp, yet even Moses cannot enter. Israel's sin still keeps them at a distance from God's holy presence, which sets up the sacrifices and priesthood of Leviticus.

translations.kjv: And Moses was not able to enter into the tent of the congregation, because the cloud abode thereon, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.

renderings.text: because the cloud settled on it
because the cloud had settled on it

translations.note: 'Abode' and 'settled' translate shakan, the verb for dwelling. The cloud does not pass by; it moves in.

translations.kjv: On the first day of the first month shalt thou set up the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation.

renderings.text: you shall erect the tabernacle of the tent of meeting
Set up the tabernacle, the tent of meeting

translations.note: The tabernacle is raised on New Year's Day, almost a year after the first Passover (12:2). God's dwelling begins a new year for his people.

steps.gospel: Exodus ends with the goal of redemption reached: the glory of God dwelling among his people. Yet even Moses could not enter. The glory was near but still guarded. The New Testament declares that the Word became flesh and tabernacled among us, full of grace and truth, and through his death the way into God's presence was opened. Now the Spirit fills believers as God's temple, and one day the dwelling of God will be with his people forever, with no veil and no distance, in a city filled with his glory.
application: Remember that God saved you so that he could dwell with you; treasure his presence.
Follow God's leading in your journeys, moving when he moves and waiting when he waits.
Finish faithfully what God has given you to do, and leave the glory to him.
Honor God's holiness even as you enjoy his nearness through Christ.
Look forward to the day when God's glory fills all things.

misapplications.claim: God's presence is limited to sacred buildings.
misapplications.correction: The tabernacle was a special, portable dwelling for Israel at a stage of redemptive history. In Christ, God dwells in his people by the Spirit (1 Corinthians 3:16), and the final goal is a whole creation filled with his glory.

misapplications.claim: The cloud means Christians should wait for visible signs before every decision.
misapplications.correction: The cloud was a unique provision for Israel in the wilderness. Believers are led by God's word and Spirit, using wisdom, prayer and counsel (Psalm 119:105; James 1:5).

contrasts.note: The book began with slaves building store cities for a tyrant and ends with a free people building a dwelling for their God.
God is near, yet his holiness still bars entrance, a tension resolved in Christ.
Israel's movement and rest are governed by God's presence.

features.label: Sevenfold obedience
features.note: 'As the LORD had commanded Moses' appears seven times in verses 16-32, completing the theme of obedience from chapter 39.

features.label: Creation echoes
features.note: New Year's Day, finishing the work and God taking up residence recall Genesis 1-2, with the tabernacle as a renewed creation.

features.label: An open ending
features.note: Exodus closes looking ahead: 'throughout all their journeys.' The story continues in Leviticus and Numbers.

features.label: From mountain to tent
features.note: The glory that rested on Sinai (24:16) now rests on the tabernacle, so God's presence can travel with Israel.

steps.summary: Exodus 40 brings the book to its goal. Moses sets up the tabernacle exactly as God commanded and finishes the work, and the cloud covers the tent as the glory of the LORD fills it. God now dwells among his redeemed people and leads them on their journey. The story points ahead to Christ, in whom God's glory tabernacled among us, and to the new creation where God dwells with his people forever.

metaArc.book: Chapter 40 is the climax of Exodus: the movement from slavery in Egypt to God's glory dwelling among his people is complete. It hands the story to Leviticus, which explains how a holy God can live among a sinful people.
metaArc.redemptive: This is Redemption reaching its goal and pointing to New Creation: God dwelling with his people, fulfilled in Christ's incarnation, the Spirit in the church, and the new Jerusalem.
